newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Investors keen to revive SAfrica Pepsi unit - paper.
newsitem.headline: Investors keen to revive SAfrica Pepsi unit - paper.

text.p: The African-American investors who backed Pepsi's abortive return to South Africa are looking for ways to revive the venture, Business Day newspaper reported on Tuesday.
This comes after the struggling soft drink firm pulled the plug on South African bottler New Age Beverages (NAB) last month.

The group of investors includes OJ Simpson defence lawyer Johnnie Cochran, actor Danny Glover, Hampton University president William Harvey and Earl Graves, publisher of Black Enterprise magazine and owner of the largest Pepsi bottling firm in the U.S.
Angered by Pepsi's sudden pullout, the group is having "discussions" with Pepsi "at the highest corporate level" and has sent a lawyer to South Africa to review the situation, Business Day reported.
"There is a belief that Pepsi remains a viable commercial proposition in South Africa," a source close to the group told the newspaper.
"The fact that (its return) was not successfully imnplemented does not mean it is not viable".
Pepsi kicked off a South African division of the global cola wars three years ago, entering the market via NAB with its eyes fixed initially on black townships, such as Soweto outside Johannesburg.
More recently the battle has been widened to a countrywide showdown between Pepsi and arch-rival Coca-Cola Corporation.
